card.heard: walk me through the API on the board
card.say: The feed call uses a cursor, so the list can keep loading without skipping posts. The response carries the posts and the next cursor together. For likes and comments, the requestId is the key part. The phone sends the same requestId when it retries, so the server can drop a duplicate. The like response returns the new count and the user's own state, so the screen can correct itself after a sync.
card.then: I'll cover what happens when an offline like conflicts with the server.

card.problem: Design the news feed for an Android app like Facebook
card.constraints: ["View list of Feed/Post", "Like Count, Comment Count, tap on Comment go to Detail Screen", "Infinite Scrolling list", "Type of Content (text, image, video)", "100 million daily users globally", "Creating posts, authentication and friends are out of scope", "Users must read cached posts, like posts and write comments offline"]
card.heard: why cursor pagination rather than page numbers
card.say: With page numbers, a new post at the top pushes everything down. So page two repeats posts the user already saw. A cursor marks the last post we got, so the next call starts right after it. It also stays correct when posts are deleted, and it works well with an infinite list.

card.heard: explain the high-level diagram, focus on the mobile client

card.problem: Design the news feed for an Android app like Facebook

card.heard: user likes then unlikes the same post offline, what to sync
card.say: The two taps cancel out, so I'd keep only the final state. When the user likes and then unlikes offline, I update the local row to "not liked" and drop the pending like. Nothing goes to the server, because the server never saw the like. If the like was already sent and confirmed, then the unlike is a new request with its own requestId. So the queue holds one final intent per post, not a list of taps.

card.heard: 200 MB cache limit and logout
card.say: I'd enforce the limit in the local store, not in the UI. The board already says 200 MB with LRU, so I'd check the size after each write and evict the least recently used posts and media until we're under the limit. On logout, I'd clear the whole store: the database, the in-memory cache and the image cache. Otherwise the next user could see the last user's posts. I'd also cancel any pending like sync, because those requests belong to the old account.

card.heard: prefetch next page without wasting data
card.say: I'd prefetch when the user is close to the end of the list, not when the page loads. I'd start it a few items before the last one, so the next page is ready before they reach it.
